Final-edit audit

What changed from the previous storyboard

Corrections to the edit map

Opening, middle, and closing now match the export

  • Opening: a brief black beat, then a fast landscape move, overhead river stones, and meadow imagery. It does not open on the finished bathroom.
  • Nature sequence: wildflowers, magnolia, forest canopy, mist, and water appear before the sketching and product-design process.
  • Product section: hand-drawn linework and tactile surface gestures lead into a warm abstract transition before the decorated basin and matching toilet are shown, around 01:05 onward.
  • Closing: the film returns to the flowering landscape. “WILD AT HEART COLLECTION” appears first, then the centered KOHLER wordmark, followed by black.
Brand / copy notes

Keep the source footage distinct from creative additions

The small KOHLER watermark appears in the upper-right corner across many shots. A separate KOHLER mark is also visible on the basin in the product-detail passage.

The closing campaign title reads “WILD AT HEART COLLECTION”. No extra performance claim is evident in the reviewed frames, so the storyboard does not add one.

Voiceover: the narration below is an optional creative draft, not a transcription of the original soundtrack. Use the source audio as the authority for music and sound already present.

03 / Visual storyboard

Scene-by-scene breakdown

Every card uses a frame extracted from the final video. Descriptions distinguish visible action and text from recommendations for a recreation or derivative film.

SOURCE FRAME · ~02s
01NATURE / OPEN
00:00–00:05 · 5 sec

A black beat, then the wide world

WHAT WE SEE

The film begins on black for a brief beat, then opens into a fast-moving alpine valley carpeted with wildflowers. A top-down view of river stones follows, before the meadow enters the frame. A small KOHLER watermark sits in the upper-right corner once imagery begins.

STORY PURPOSE

Make nature the first protagonist. The opening establishes scale, motion, and the visual world that will later be translated into botanical product artwork.

CAMERA / EDIT

Use the fast forward glide through the valley as the first motion cue; cut to the more graphic overhead stone texture. Keep the opening brisk but not chaotic.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No centered opening end-card. KOHLER appears as a small corner watermark over the landscape.

SOUND DIRECTION

Suggested direction: a low airy swell from black into open space, then a restrained organic score. Match the speed of the landscape push-in.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“Before form, there is nature.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~08s
02BOTANICAL / COLOR
00:05–00:10 · 5 sec

Petals caught in backlight

WHAT WE SEE

The meadow gives way to small pink wildflowers, a single yellow flower glowing against an amber backlight, and pale magnolia blossoms. The palette changes from cool open landscape to warm, luminous botanical detail.

STORY PURPOSE

Introduce the campaign’s key natural references: petal edges, delicate centers, warm highlights, and gentle color contrast.

CAMERA / EDIT

Macro close-ups, shallow depth of field, backlit petals, and a restrained lens flare. Hold long enough for the flower silhouette to read.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

The KOHLER corner watermark remains visible; no added claim or feature copy appears in this passage.

SOUND DIRECTION

Keep the music airy. Any light outdoor ambience should sit below the score and should not sound like a literal nature documentary.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“In every petal, light finds a new shape.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~14s
03NATURE / ATMOSPHERE
00:10–00:19 · 9 sec

Canopy, mist, and moving water

WHAT WE SEE

The film moves through layered green canopy and backlit leaves into a misty forest floor, then opens onto water reflecting the last light. Nature alternates between close botanical detail and wider, atmospheric environments.

STORY PURPOSE

Build a calm, immersive world of forest greens, soft haze, and water glints. This becomes the color and texture foundation of the collection story.

CAMERA / EDIT

Use slow gliding landscape shots and a few intimate plant details. Allow the lighter water reflections to emerge from the darker forest rather than cutting abruptly.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

Small KOHLER watermark in the upper-right corner across the environmental imagery.

SOUND DIRECTION

Suggested direction: widen the score here with a soft sustained layer; use wind or water textures sparingly.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“Through leaves, mist, and moving water, the world finds its rhythm.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~22s
04BOTANICAL / MOTIFS
00:19–00:29 · 10 sec

A bloom, a ripple, a line

WHAT WE SEE

A saturated pink flower fills the frame; a white water lily rests on dark water as circular ripples spread around it. Blossoming branches and delicate fern shapes extend the sequence from flower to water to leaf.

STORY PURPOSE

Establish the repeatable motifs that recur on the basin: petal contours, fine lines, organic curves, and circular water patterns.

CAMERA / EDIT

Alternate macro and medium-wide nature images. The water lily and ripple are a natural graphic match for rounded ceramic forms and a central drain detail later in the film.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No feature copy; the corner watermark persists.

SOUND DIRECTION

Let the score breathe between images. A subtle water accent could support the lily/ripple shot if it blends naturally with the source mix.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“A bloom. A ripple. A line carried by the wind.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~31s
05NATURE / THRESHOLD
00:29–00:34 · 5 sec

The landscape framed by a window

WHAT WE SEE

A mountain meadow and sunlit tree are framed by a window. The interior window mullions turn the natural landscape into a composed picture, suggesting the transition from observing nature to bringing its forms indoors.

STORY PURPOSE

Create a visual threshold between the exterior world and the designed bathroom environment without jumping directly to a product feature.

CAMERA / EDIT

Hold the architectural framing steady and balanced. Let the window create structure around the landscape; avoid excessive camera movement.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

The KOHLER corner watermark remains present.

SOUND DIRECTION

A gentle musical transition is enough; do not over-score the window as a dramatic reveal.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“Keep the feeling of the wild a little closer.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~39s
06DESIGN / DRAWING
00:34–00:43 · 9 sec

Nature becomes a drawing

WHAT WE SEE

A hand sketches a botanical motif on paper. Magnolia details are intercut with close views of a pencil following the flower’s contours, moving from the living reference to a carefully drawn line pattern.

STORY PURPOSE

Show the design translation clearly: nature is not merely a mood reference; its shapes become a deliberate graphic language.

CAMERA / EDIT

Use overhead or close over-the-shoulder framing for the pencil and paper. Favor shallow focus, visible graphite lines, and slow movement along the curve.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No additional super is visible in the sketch passage; KOHLER remains as a small corner mark in many shots.

SOUND DIRECTION

Suggested direction: a very quiet pencil-on-paper texture can add tactility, but keep it subordinate to the music.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“Observed, sketched, and reimagined by hand.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~46s
07SURFACE ART / CRAFT
00:43–00:49 · 6 sec

The line becomes a surface

WHAT WE SEE

A hand traces a fine botanical motif, followed by a fuller view of floral linework. The design reads as layered grey and warm copper/rose-gold lines across a pale ground, with large petals and fine internal detail.

STORY PURPOSE

Make the signature surface pattern legible. This is the bridge between a pencil sketch and the decorated sanitaryware seen later.

CAMERA / EDIT

Move from hand-and-tool detail to a flatter, more graphic view of the completed pattern. A match cut along a petal line will emphasize continuity.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No feature claims; the KOHLER corner watermark remains in the footage.

SOUND DIRECTION

A tiny tactile drawing accent is optional. The visual should communicate precision without relying on literal workshop sound.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“The language of nature takes a new form.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~52s
08TACTILE / PRODUCT USE
00:49–00:55 · 6 sec

Hands meet the decorated ceramic

WHAT WE SEE

Hands trace the illustrated surface, then a cleaning pad or sponge moves across the floral-decorated basin. The pattern is now clearly integrated with a usable product rather than remaining a drawing on paper.

STORY PURPOSE

Shift from inspiration and craft toward touch and everyday use. The gesture makes the ceramic surface feel tangible and lived-in.

CAMERA / EDIT

Close overhead framing and a slow, deliberate hand movement. Keep the product artwork visible beneath and around the hand.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No explicit cleaning-performance claim is displayed in this moment; avoid adding one unless separately verified.

SOUND DIRECTION

A soft contact sound may ground the gesture, but avoid exaggerated scrubbing effects.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

“Designed to be seen. Made to be experienced.”

SOURCE FRAME · ~57s
09ABSTRACT / MATERIAL
00:55–01:01 · 6 sec

Warm light and suspended particles

WHAT WE SEE

A glowing, rectangular form appears in a dark, warm environment, surrounded by floating amber particles. The image then softens into a field of golden bokeh before the film returns to the white product surface.

STORY PURPOSE

Provide a stylized visual pause between tactile process imagery and the cleaner product reveal. It adds warmth and contrast to the otherwise botanical palette.

CAMERA / EDIT

Use a low, close view of the illuminated form, then let the frame simplify into abstract particles. Treat it as a visual metaphor; the footage alone does not establish a specific manufacturing step.

ON-SCREEN TEXT / BRAND

No legible feature copy; the KOHLER corner mark is still visible.

SOUND DIRECTION

Let the score carry this transition. A soft low-frequency swell or delicate shimmer may underline the glow without suggesting a literal furnace recording.

OPTIONAL PROPOSED VO

No voiceover recommended; give the image a moment to breathe.

04 / Visual art direction

Color, lighting, material, and product finish

This mood board translates the final cut’s observed palette into practical references for recreating the style in CGI, photography, or AI-assisted video. The images are sampled from this final export.

Nature × surface art × ceramic

Keep the visual world organic and tactile: cool forest depth, soft flower tones, pale ceramic, delicate copper/rose-gold linework, and a warm abstract light bridge.

01 / NATURE BASE

Forest green + cool mist

Layered canopy, dark moss, backlit leaves, and softened green haze. Keep the greens rich but retain shadow detail.

02 / FLORAL ACCENT

Wildflower pink + magnolia ivory

Petal pinks and ivory blossoms supply the gentle color accent. Allow warm centers and soft backlight; avoid oversaturated candy pink.

03 / WATER + LIGHT

Deep teal + silver ripples

Dark water and small specular ripples provide cool contrast to the warm bathroom scenes and echo circular basin details.

04 / SIGNATURE ART

Fine botanical linework

Fine grey and copper/rose-gold outlines on a pale ground. Preserve negative space so the floral pattern supports the product silhouette.

05 / WARM TRANSITION

Amber glow + floating particles

Use as a short abstract warmth cue. It is a stylized visual bridge; do not represent it as a confirmed process shot without production confirmation.

06 / CERAMIC FORM

Gloss white + rose-gold fitting

A clean white basin, visible rim and drain, floral artwork, and warm metal faucet. Long soft reflections should reveal the ceramic curve without clipping highlights.

07 / COLLECTION COHESION

Matching decorated sanitaryware

Repeat the floral art across coordinated products. Keep the surrounding blush stone and neutral accessories quiet enough for the surface motif to remain legible.

08 / FINISHED INTERIOR

Blush, ivory, pale stone

Ribbed vanity, pale stone top, illuminated mirror, warm metal, and window daylight complete the premium bathroom setting.

Suggested visual balance

For a recreated product film, lead with natural greens and landscape atmosphere, then use ivory/stone as the product base. Reserve pink and coppery metallic linework for flower references and the decorated surface; use amber only as a short transition accent.

Shape and finish notes

Keep the basin silhouette soft and sculptural with a clean rim and generous bowl. Let long, soft reflections reveal the gloss. Keep the floral lines delicate and low-relief in appearance; the rose-gold faucet should feel warm, not orange. Avoid hard clipped highlights on white ceramic.

Lighting

Nature: backlight through leaves, misty depth, water sparkle, and sun flare. Product: large diffused sources with controlled strip highlights on the rim and faucet. Abstract bridge: darker field, warm amber glow, tiny particle glints. Interior: soft daylight plus the oval mirror’s gentle practical glow.

Surface-art and composition

Use a fine-line botanical motif with grey and copper/rose-gold strokes on a pale ground. At macro scale, show line quality and finish; at overhead scale, show the pattern in relation to the drain and bowl. Keep countertop accessories few and subdued.

05 / Script option

Optional voiceover, timed to the final cut

A restrained, poetic narration for a new adaptation of this edit. It is deliberately not a feature list and should leave room for the original music, visible campaign title, and brand mark.

Direction: warm, close, unhurried delivery; leave breath between phrases. Do not speak over the final title and logo hold.

06 / Production notes

What to preserve when recreating the style

1. Visual rhymes

Petal → drawn petal; water ripple → circular basin detail; landscape → window view; pencil stroke → finished floral decoration. Make the match cuts feel intentional, not decorative.

2. Editing rhythm

Begin with faster landscape movement, let the flora and mist breathe, tighten slightly during drawing and hands, then slow again for the hero basin and final campaign landscape.

3. Product clarity

After the artwork is established, show enough clean basin, faucet, toilet, and interior views that the design remains a product advertisement—not only a nature montage.

Final delivery checklist

Match the final runtime (about 01:41), retain the 16:9 composition, keep the small upper-right KOHLER watermark where present in the source, preserve the end-title typography, and allow the final KOHLER wordmark to resolve before the fade to black. Confirm exact frame-level cut points against the edit timeline before production.
